highlights: Teams: link your PeckBoard with your coworkers' servers under Settings → Teams. No accounts to create.
Invite a server with a one-time link. Before you approve it, you and your coworker compare a six-digit code, so a forwarded or leaked link cannot get anyone in.
Owners and admins manage who is in the team; your server checks every change itself instead of trusting the service that passes it along.
Agents now keep long-term memory for each folder: architecture, design decisions, code structure and your working rules. Every session in that folder starts out knowing it.
Short-term memory holds what an agent is working on right now and clears itself after 24 hours. You can change how long it lasts in Settings → Chat.
The Memory dialog has a new Long-term tab where you can read, add, edit and delete what a folder's agents remember.
Codex now lists the models your Codex account actually offers, including new ones as soon as OpenAI adds them, instead of an old built-in list.
Publishing a skill to Peckboard Public now takes one click: it goes straight to skills.peckboard.com, no pull request needed.
Fork anyone's public skill, make it your own, and ask its author to merge your changes back.
Skill authors see incoming merge requests in Settings → Skills, with the changes side by side, and can merge them as a new version.
Every public skill now has a History tab showing each version and what changed.
A new Welcome page helps you get going on your first launch.
"Try it now" gives you a ready-made first task, so you can see an agent at work in one click.
Starter prompts suggest things to ask when you open a new chat.
A demo project shows how cards, workers and the board fit together.
Scan a QR code to open PeckBoard on your phone.
Experimental plugins now carry a badge, so you know what is still being tried out.
When a long chat outgrows the model's memory ("Prompt is too long"), it now carries on by itself with a fresh start, keeping a summary of what came before.
Skills: reusable instructions you can give an agent. Keep them for yourself, share them with your team through git, or pick from the public catalog.
Choose which skills a session uses from its menu, or when you start it.
Updates now wait until nothing is running before restarting.
